ease off: get less strong or bad (something unpleasant)
typical: rain/traffic/pain eases off. NOT for: getting worse.
The rain had eased off a bit.
Wait until the traffic eases off.
stop being so demanding or unpleasant to someone
typical: ease off (on sb). NOT for: pressuring.
The boss eased off on the staff.
Ease off a bit; he's trying.
ease up: work less hard or with less energy
typical: ease up a little, ease up on sb. NOT for: pushing harder.
Just relax and ease up a little.
He eased up after the exam.
typical: ease up on sth. NOT for: increasing.
You should ease up on the whisky.
improve or lessen (weather, traffic or pain)
typical: snow/rain eases up. NOT for: worsening.
eat out: have a meal in a restaurant instead of at home
typical: eat out tonight/every week. NOT for: cooking at home.
eat up: finish all the food on your plate
typical: Eat up!, eat sth up. NOT for: leaving food.
use a lot of something (time, money or resources)
typical: eat up time/money/resources. NOT for: saving.
The project is eating up our budget.
Long commutes eat up my time.
egg on: encourage someone to do something unwise or unwanted
typical: egg sb on (to do sth). NOT for: discouraging.
His friends kept egging him on.
She egged him on to jump.
end in: typical: end in divorce/failure/tears/a draw. NOT for: starting with.
One in three marriages ends in divorce.
The match ended in a draw.
it will end in tears (BrE spoken)
typical: it'll end in tears. NOT for: happy endings.
Don't play with fire; it'll end in tears.
It will all end in tears.
end up: finally be in a situation, place or state, often unplanned
typical: end up + -ing/place/as/with. NOT for: planned results.
We ended up having a meal together.
Where will the pictures end up?
finally become something after a series of events
typical: end up as/with sth. NOT for: starting a job.
He could end up as president.
enter into: officially start an agreement or discussion
typical: enter into an agreement/contract/talks. NOT for: leaving.
The council entered into an agreement.
typical: enter into the spirit of it. NOT for: staying out.
She entered into the spirit of the party.
even out: become or make something more level or equal
typical: things even out, even sth out. NOT for: growing uneven.
Use a brush to even out the colour.
